input.prompt: Simulate the thermal conductivity of a Lennard-Jones (LJ) system in LAMMPS. Define a simulation box with dimensions 10×10×20 in reduced LJ units. Set the number density of the fluid to 0.6 and the initial temperature to 1.35 in LJ units. Use a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice to initialize atomic positions and assign a Lennard-Jones potential with a cutoff of 2.5σ. Create two temperature-controlled regions: a hot region at the bottom (z = 0 to 1) and a cold region at the top (z = 10 to 11). First, equilibrate the system using the NVT ensemble at 1.35 temperature for 1000 timesteps with a temperature damping factor of 0.5, then switch to the NVE ensemble while applying Langevin thermostats to the hot and cold regions to maintain temperatures at 1.70 and 1.0, respectively, using damping factor of 1.0 for both thermostats. Track the energy added and removed by the thermostats and compute the temperature difference between the regions. Run the simulation for 10,000 timesteps to establish a steady-state temperature gradient. Afterward, reset the Langevin energy accumulation and continue the simulation for an additional 20,000 timesteps while calculating the running average of the temperature difference. Divide the simulation box into bins along the z-direction and compute the temperature profile over time. Use the heat flux and steady-state temperature gradient to compute the thermal conductivity using Fourier’s law. As the final output, return the thermal conductivity in Lennard-Jones (LJ) reduced units.

Define a simulation box with dimensions 10×10×20 in reduced LJ units. Set the number density of the fluid to 0.6 and the initial temperature to 1.35 in LJ units. Use a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice to initialize atomic positions and assign a Lennard-Jones potential with a cutoff of 2.5σ. Create two temperature-controlled regions: a hot region at the bottom (z = 0 to 1) and a cold region at the top (z = 10 to 11). Save this structure using the write_data command in LAMMPS data format. As the final output, return the absolute path of the structure file.

Read the structure file and equilibrate the Lennard-Jones fluid system. Use the NVT ensemble to maintain the system at a constant temperature of 1.35 in LJ units with a damping parameter of 0.5. Run the equilibration for 1000 timesteps while monitoring system properties such as temperature. Save the structure after this step. As the final output, return the absolute path of the updated structure file.

Stabilize the equilibrated Lennard-Jones fluid system in LAMMPS. Read the structure file from the previous equilibration step. NVE ensemble while applying Langevin thermostats to the hot and cold regions to maintain temperatures at 1.70 and 1.0, respectively, using damping factor of 1.0 for both thermostats. Track the energy added and removed by the thermostats and compute the temperature difference between the regions. Run the simulation for 10,000 timesteps to establish a steady-state temperature gradient. Save the final structure file. As the final output, return the absolute path of the updated structure file.

Read the stabilized system structure from the previous step. Apply Langevin thermostats to the hot and cold regions with target temperatures of 1.70 and 1.00, respectively. Use a damping parameter of 1.0. Define 1D binning along the z-direction with a bin size of 0.05. Run the simulation for 20,000 timesteps. Compute a running average of the temperature difference and use it to calculate thermal conductivity. Use the heat flux and steady-state temperature gradient to compute the thermal conductivity using Fourier’s law. As the final output, return the computed thermal conductivity value in Lennard-Jones (LJ) units.
